llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Dataify integration for submitting Facebook profile collection tasks, with expected token and network use for that purpose.

dimensions.detail: The skill submits Facebook personal profile collection jobs to Dataify and returns task status; this is privacy-sensitive but clearly matches the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The workflow asks the user to review parameters before submission and restricts URLs to https://www.facebook.com/, though implicit invocation is enabled for related scraping/collection requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Artifacts are limited to instructions, icons, an agent metadata file, and a Python helper script; no package install, hidden loader, or obfuscated setup behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The helper script reads DATAIFY_API_TOKEN and sends authorized POST requests to Dataify, which is proportionate and disclosed for a Dataify task-submission skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill may help the user save DATAIFY_API_TOKEN, but it tells the agent to ask first and have the user run the command; it does not silently persist credentials.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to submit Facebook profile collection jobs through Dataify. Be aware that it can use a saved DATAIFY_API_TOKEN and send profile URLs to Dataify, so confirm the target URLs and make sure you have authorization and a legitimate basis for collecting the profile data.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Environment token access and outbound Dataify requests are necessary for submitting authenticated Builder tasks and are disclosed in SKILL.md and the script.
[SQP-1] expected: Implicit invocation is enabled, but the trigger language is tied to Facebook profile collection, token configuration, task status, and troubleshooting rather than unrelated behavior.
[EA2] expected: Using an existing DATAIFY_API_TOKEN avoids asking the user to re-enter a token; the workflow still requires parameter review before submission and requires confirmation before saving a new token.
